headline: Ex-air force officer found dead in Turag river
summary: The body of retired Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri was recovered from the river in Tongi after he went missing for a day.
details: The body of retired Bangladesh Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri was recovered from the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon.
Tongi River Police carried out the recovery operation after the officer had been missing for a day.
A duty officer at Uttarkhan Police Station confirmed the recovery of the body on Thursday morning.
Reports from various quarters suggest that Tahsif had released a video showing ousted minister Sheikh Hasina fleeing by aircraft on August 5, 2024.
caption:
A retired Air Force officer's body was found in the Turag River after he went missing for a day.

The body of retired Bangladesh Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri was recovered from the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon.

Tongi River Police carried out the recovery operation after the officer had been missing for a day.

A duty officer at Uttarkhan Police Station confirmed the recovery of the body on Thursday morning.

Reports from various quarters suggest that Tahsif had released a video showing ousted minister Sheikh Hasina fleeing by aircraft on August 5, 2024.

headline: Bangladesh reach U-15 World Cup quarterfinals after penalty win
summary: The youth team beat Singapore 4-3 on penalties to secure a spot in the final eight of FIFA’s inaugural U-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan.
details: Bangladesh secured a place in the quarterfinals of FIFA’s inaugural U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, after defeating Singapore 4-3 on penalties.
The round of 16 match at the Hovsan Competition Complex ended 1-1 after regulation time before the Bangladeshi side prevailed in the shootout.
This victory follows a similar path in the round of 32, where Bangladesh beat Seychelles 4-2 on penalties after a 1-1 draw.
Bangladesh will now face Montenegro in the quarterfinals. Montenegro has also advanced through two penalty shootouts to reach this stage.
The inaugural FIFA tournament features youth teams from 191 countries, played with 8-a-side teams on smaller pitches with 20-minute halves.
In the group stage, Bangladesh was placed in Group G with Portugal, Indonesia, Fiji, Burundi, and Wales, winning their final match against Fiji 3-1.
With the wins over Seychelles and Singapore, Bangladesh has now won three of their seven matches in the tournament so far.
caption:
From the round of 32 to the round of 16, Bangladesh has fought through two penalty shootouts to reach the quarterfinals!

Bangladesh secured a place in the quarterfinals of FIFA’s inaugural U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, after defeating Singapore 4-3 on penalties.

The round of 16 match at the Hovsan Competition Complex ended 1-1 after regulation time before the Bangladeshi side prevailed in the shootout.

This victory follows a similar path in the round of 32, where Bangladesh beat Seychelles 4-2 on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Bangladesh will now face Montenegro in the quarterfinals. Montenegro has also advanced through two penalty shootouts to reach this stage.

The inaugural FIFA tournament features youth teams from 191 countries, played with 8-a-side teams on smaller pitches with 20-minute halves.

In the group stage, Bangladesh was placed in Group G with Portugal, Indonesia, Fiji, Burundi, and Wales, winning their final match against Fiji 3-1.

With the wins over Seychelles and Singapore, Bangladesh has now won three of their seven matches in the tournament so far.
